why: B has four conjuncts. Its first three (j injective, exactness at ker(T ⊕ φ) and at ℝᵏ) are pure linear algebra for any T and φ and are proved outright (B_alg_part, without A). The content is the fourth: c is onto under (P), read as general position of the slice F_t = (f − S) + Σ λᵢ σᵢ at (0, x) over ℝᵏ × X in SOME tame chart, with the conclusion in EVERY chart point p. A (lemma_6_31) needs hypotheses that B does not give. (i) S and the sᵢ must be sc⁺-sections of π*P → ℝⁿ × X on the whole space; B's S is any map with (f − S)(x) = 0 and its σᵢ are any sections. (ii) A needs an sc-smooth curve Φ of zeros of f + S(q', ·) through x. (iii) A needs F'(0, (q, x)) onto for the whole family over ℝᵏ × ℝⁿ × X. All are satisfiable: (i) with global sections, (ii) with n = 0 and Φ constant, and (iii) from (P) by chart transfer, once the sections are sc-smooth. With n = 0 and sc⁺ sections, A ⇒ B would be glue (moving from ℝᵏ × X to ℝᵏ × ℝ⁰ × X and from sectionDiff to sectionAdd). Without the smoothness, B's T = linAt in p is the junk value 0 whenever f − S is not sc¹ on all of p.c.U, so A cannot reach B's generality. B ⇒ A fails in content: B's surjectivity needs the general position of the slice (a tame chart and an sc-complement of the kernel in the reduced tangent space), which A's hypothesis (only F' onto, plus Φ) does not give. B also says nothing about T ∈ Lin(f, x) or about the identification ker F_t'(φ(t), 0) = J(ker(T ⊕ φ)): B takes ker(T ⊕ φ) as the middle term by definition. B_to_A is proved only vacuously, by re-running the proof of lemma_6_31 from the non-item lemmas exists_sliceKernel and lemma_6_14.
B_issue: B's surjectivity conjunct is believed false in B's generality (not formalized). S and σᵢ are arbitrary, and the general position is in some tame chart while the conclusion is in every chart point p. Take f − S sc-smooth near x but not sc¹ on the whole domain of p.c. Then linAt in p is the junk 0, so c must map ℝᵏ onto K_z, which fails, e.g., for k = 0 and a nonzero fibre. Meanwhile F_t can be in general position in a small tame chart around (0, x). The text's s(·, t) and sᵢ(·, t) are sc⁺, so the text's statement is not affected; B dropped the smoothness of S and σᵢ ('their sc⁺-property is not used by the claim'), but the chart-level linearization does use it.
overlap: 828 shared project theorems, all from the vacuous B_to_A, which re-runs lemma_6_31's own proof: exists_sliceKernel with its parts exists_sliceOps, mem_linSet_sectionAdd_pullbackSlice, surjective_coprod_of_isLinSurjAt (with fderiv_mem_linKer and IsLinSurjAt.linAt_surjective) and linKer_inf_ker_sliceProj_eq_map, plus lemma_6_14 and the sc-calculus and product-chart infrastructure under them. B_alg_part uses no project theorem beyond the definitions.
